## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-7-2-trajectory-analysis-using-slingshot/>

Part 1 of 3. Slingshot is an alternative to Monocle 3 (tutorial 7) for
trajectory inference. It works on a low-dimensional embedding (here UMAP) and
cluster labels: it builds a minimum spanning tree between clusters to define
**lineages**, then fits a smooth **principal curve** along each lineage, giving
every cell a pseudotime per lineage and a weight for each lineage.

The article applies Slingshot to a single biologically related lineage rather
than to all PBMC cell types together. Mature, terminally differentiated PBMC
types (B cells, monocytes) are not on a common differentiation path with T/NK
cells, so forcing them into one trajectory gives a misleading result. Here the
T/NK lineage (`params$lineage.celltypes`) is analysed.

This notebook: loads the annotated Seurat object from tutorial 4, downsamples
each cell type, subsets to the lineage, and converts it to a
`SingleCellExperiment`. Part 2 runs Slingshot; part 3 validates the trajectory
and finds trajectory-associated genes.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 1-6). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------

# Core trajectory analysis
library(slingshot)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(princurve)
library(TrajectoryUtils)

# Single-cell analysis infrastructure
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Data manipulation
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Visualization
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(scales)
library(grDevices)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_7-2_trajectory_slingshot/tut7-2_trajectory_slingshot_part1.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
traj.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$traj.subdir)

# Create organized output directories
for (d in c("plots", "plots/trajectories", "plots/pseudotime", "results")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(traj.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(traj.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Column names, condition levels and colors from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
cluster.col <- params$cluster.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
condition.colors <- setNames(unlist(params$condition.palette), unlist(params$condition.levels))

cat("Environment setup complete!\n")
cat("Slingshot version:", as.character(packageVersion("slingshot")), "\n")
cat("Seurat version:", as.character(packageVersion("Seurat")), "\n")
```

## Understanding the Slingshot workflow

1. Load the annotated Seurat object (tutorial 4)
2. Downsample cells (10% per cell type for tutorial efficiency)
3. Subset to the lineage and convert Seurat -> SingleCellExperiment (SCE)
4. Run Slingshot trajectory inference (part 2)
5. Extract lineages and pseudotime (part 2)
6. Visualize trajectories and curves (part 2)
7. Identify trajectory-associated genes (part 3)
8. Integrate results back to Seurat (part 3)

## Load the annotated Seurat object from tutorial 4

```{r step2_load_obj}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 2: Load annotated Seurat object from Part 4
#-----------------------------------------------

# Load the complete annotated object
annotated.file <- file.path(base.dir, params$annot.subdir, params$annotated.rds)
cat("Reading in annotated Seurat object:", annotated.file, "\n")
seurat_full <- readRDS(annotated.file)

stopifnot(all(c(celltype.col, cluster.col, sample.col, condition.col) %in% colnames(seurat_full@meta.data)))

# Verify data structure
cat("Original dataset:\n")
cat("  Total cells:", ncol(seurat_full), "\n")
cat("  Total genes:", nrow(seurat_full), "\n")
cat("  Samples:", length(unique(seurat_full@meta.data[[sample.col]])), "\n")
cat("  Cell types:", length(unique(seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]])), "\n\n")

# Check cell type distribution
cat("Cell type distribution (full dataset):\n")
cell_type_counts <- table(seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]])
print(cell_type_counts)
cat("\n")

# Check which UMAP reduction is available
available_reductions <- names(seurat_full@reductions)
cat("Available reductions:", paste(available_reductions, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Strategic downsampling: maintaining biological diversity

Sampling a fixed fraction from every cell type keeps all cell types represented
(sampling at random from the whole dataset can lose rare types) while reducing
computation.

```{r step3_downsample}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 3: Downsample to a fraction of cells per cell type (exclude rare types)
#-----------------------------------------------

# Set seed for reproducible downsampling
set.seed(params$seed)

# Get unique cell types and exclude rare cell types (Platelets in the article;
# too rare)
all_cell_types <- unique(seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]])
cell_types <- all_cell_types[!all_cell_types %in% unlist(params$exclude.celltypes)]

cat("Cell types to analyze (excluding ", paste(unlist(params$exclude.celltypes), collapse = ", "), "):\n", sep = "")
print(cell_types)
cat("\n")

# Sample a fraction from each cell type independently
downsampled_cells <- c()

for (cell_type in cell_types) {
  # Get all cells of this type
  cells_of_type <- colnames(seurat_full)[seurat_full@meta.data[[celltype.col]] == cell_type]

  # Calculate fraction (with a minimum number of cells for rare types)
  n_sample <- max(params$downsample.min_cells, round(length(cells_of_type) * params$downsample.fraction))

  # Don't sample more cells than exist
  n_sample <- min(n_sample, length(cells_of_type))

  # Random sample
  sampled <- sample(cells_of_type, n_sample)
  downsampled_cells <- c(downsampled_cells, sampled)

  cat(sprintf("  %s: %d → %d cells (%.1f%%)\n",
              cell_type, length(cells_of_type), n_sample,
              100 * n_sample / length(cells_of_type)))
}

# Create downsampled Seurat object
seurat_subset <- subset(seurat_full, cells = downsampled_cells)

cat("\n")
cat("Downsampled dataset:\n")
cat("  Total cells:", ncol(seurat_subset), "\n")
cat("  Cell types retained:", length(unique(seurat_subset@meta.data[[celltype.col]])), "\n")
cat("  Reduction from full:",
    round(100 * (1 - ncol(seurat_subset)/ncol(seurat_full)), 1), "%\n\n")

# Verify cell type representation
cat("Cell type distribution (downsampled):\n")
print(table(seurat_subset@meta.data[[celltype.col]]))
```

## Visualize the downsampled dataset

```{r step4_overview, fig.width = 16, fig.height = 12}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 4: Visualize downsampled data
#-----------------------------------------------

# Determine which UMAP to use (from Part 3 integration)
umap_reduction <- intersect(unlist(params$umap.priority), names(seurat_subset@reductions))[1]
if (is.na(umap_reduction)) stop("None of params$umap.priority found in object reductions: ",
                                paste(names(seurat_subset@reductions), collapse = ", "))

cat("Using UMAP reduction:", umap_reduction, "\n\n")

# Create multi-panel overview
p1 <- DimPlot(seurat_subset, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = celltype.col, label = TRUE,
              label.size = 3.5, pt.size = 0.8, repel = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Cell Types (Downsampled Data)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "right")

p2 <- DimPlot(seurat_subset, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = condition.col, pt.size = 0.8) +
  ggtitle("Condition Distribution") +
  scale_color_manual(values = condition.colors) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

p3 <- DimPlot(seurat_subset, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = cluster.col, label = TRUE,
              pt.size = 0.8) +
  ggtitle("Seurat Clusters") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.position = "right")

# Combine plots
p_overview <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | plot_spacer())
print(p_overview)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/01_downsampled_data_overview.png"), p_overview,
       width = 16, height = 12, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Critical decision: choose the right analysis strategy

Analysing every PBMC cell type in one trajectory would force unrelated
terminally differentiated cell types (B cells, monocytes, T/NK cells) onto a
single path; the resulting "pseudotime" would reflect lineage identity rather
than a biological process. The strategy used here is a **cell-type-specific
trajectory**: choose a biologically related lineage, subset to it, and run
Slingshot on that subset.

## Subset to the lineage

```{r step5_subset_lineage, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 5: Subset to T/NK cell lineage
#-----------------------------------------------

# Define T/NK cell types
t_nk_types <- unlist(params$lineage.celltypes)

# Subset Seurat object
seurat_t_nk <- seurat_subset[, seurat_subset@meta.data[[celltype.col]] %in% t_nk_types]

cat("T/NK lineage subset:\n")
cat("  Total cells:", ncol(seurat_t_nk), "\n")
cat("  Cell types:", length(unique(seurat_t_nk@meta.data[[celltype.col]])), "\n\n")

# Cell type distribution
cat("Cell type distribution in T/NK subset:\n")
print(table(seurat_t_nk@meta.data[[celltype.col]]))
cat("\n")

# Visualize T/NK subset
p_t_nk_subset <- DimPlot(seurat_t_nk,
                         reduction = umap_reduction,
                         group.by = celltype.col,
                         label = TRUE,
                         pt.size = 1) +
  ggtitle("T/NK Cell Lineage Subset") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
print(p_t_nk_subset)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/02_t_nk_subset.png"), p_t_nk_subset,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Convert the subset to SingleCellExperiment

```{r step6_convert_sce}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 6: Convert T/NK subset to SingleCellExperiment
#-----------------------------------------------

# Convert Seurat to SCE (preserves all data, metadata, and reductions)
sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seurat_t_nk)

cat("Created SingleCellExperiment object for T/NK lineage:\n")
cat("  Cells:", ncol(sce), "\n")
cat("  Genes:", nrow(sce), "\n")
cat("  Assays:", paste(assayNames(sce), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("  Reduced dimensions:", paste(reducedDimNames(sce), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("  Cell metadata columns:", ncol(colData(sce)), "\n\n")

# Verify critical components transferred
cat("Verifying transferred information:\n")
cat("  Expression data (counts):", "counts" %in% assayNames(sce), "\n")
cat("  Expression data (logcounts):", "logcounts" %in% assayNames(sce), "\n")
cat("  Cell types (", celltype.col, "):",
    celltype.col %in% colnames(colData(sce)), "\n")
cat("  Clusters (", cluster.col, "):",
    cluster.col %in% colnames(colData(sce)), "\n\n")

# Extract UMAP coordinates using the reduction determined in Step 4
# When converting Seurat to SCE, reduction names become uppercase
# e.g., "umap.cca" becomes "UMAP.CCA"
sce_umap_name <- toupper(umap_reduction)

cat("UMAP reduction from Seurat:", umap_reduction, "\n")
cat("SCE reduction name:", sce_umap_name, "\n")
cat("Available in SCE:", sce_umap_name %in% reducedDimNames(sce), "\n\n")

# Extract UMAP coordinates
umap_coords <- reducedDim(sce, sce_umap_name)

cat("UMAP coordinates:\n")
cat("  Dimensions:", dim(umap_coords), "\n")
cat("  Range X:", round(range(umap_coords[,1]), 2), "\n")
cat("  Range Y:", round(range(umap_coords[,2]), 2), "\n\n")

# Create standardized "UMAP" entry for Slingshot
# Slingshot expects reducedDim to be named "UMAP"
reducedDim(sce, "UMAP") <- umap_coords
```

The SingleCellExperiment structure: `assays()` holds expression matrices
(counts, logcounts, ...), `colData()` cell metadata, `rowData()` gene metadata
and `reducedDims()` dimensionality reductions (PCA, UMAP, ...).

saveRDS(seurat_t_nk, file.path(traj.dir, "results/seurat_T_NK_subset.rds"))
